title: Google says India data center will use air cooling amid water fears
source_used: AFP text as carried by Kuwait Times
key_facts: Google says its 'gigawatt-scale' AI data center in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh, India, will use air cooling instead of water after residents objected in an area already short of water.
The site is part of a 15 billion dollar investment, is due to open in 2028 and will be Google's biggest AI hub outside the United States.

Alexander Smith, Google's head of infrastructure and energy for Asia-Pacific, told AFP the water assessment 'pointed to pressure on the local watershed' and that this shaped the cooling choice from the outset.

Google says it will replenish 120 percent of the freshwater it uses by 2030, pays the full cost of required grid upgrades and plans new clean-energy projects in Visakhapatnam; it does not disclose power capacity for individual sites.
Activists demand a moratorium on new data centers across Andhra Pradesh until more is known about their effects.
Smith projects about 688 million dollars a year in local economic activity and says each Google data-center job supports nine more locally.
In Finland, authorities recently ordered work to stop on two Google data center sites pending mandatory environmental assessments.
quote_evidence: Google says its massive new data center in the Indian city of Visakhapatnam will use air cooling instead of water, after residents objected to the impact of the project on the environment and their lives in an area already facing water shortages.
Google does not disclose power capacity figures for individual sites, but Smith said it pays the full cost of required grid upgrades and plans to invest in new clean energy projects in Visakhapatnam.
why_it_matters_hint: A big tech firm changes its cooling plan in response to local water fears, but activists still want a pause.
notes: Company statement to AFP, not independently checked. Pool marks this a follow-up of The Hindu's 9 Oct item (India data centre boom sparks protests over water, power and environment), which was in the 10 Oct pool only and not in our 10 Oct Full Report; only its headline was seen. Kuwait Times carries the AFP text, so AFP is the source.
